guidelines.detail: same as LRN-017 (The generated model ends the branches for closing, paid, and forwarding outcomes directly on end events with the action in the label (X5, X8). The reference has a task for each named action before the end event (M1, M2, M7). The description states these actions explicitly (S4, S6, S7). The failure is the same as the one LRN-017 and LRN-032 already address, so the new guideline duplicates a learned)

same as LRN-032 (The generated model places the outcome into the end event label ("Case closed (paid)") and omits the stated booking and closing tasks (M3, M2, X5). The learned guideline LRN-032 already requires a closing action to be its own task before the end event, and LRN-013 and LRN-017 cover the related rules for own actions after waited occurrences. The proposed rule restates that existing requirement for )

refines COL-07 (The reference model has no pools or message flows. The generated model added pools for an outside party and a receiving agency, plus message flows to them, although the description only has the company send a request or forward a case. COL-07 covers ordinary internal roles, not outside parties, so this guideline adds the case of external recipients and keeps the company's process as the only model)

refines GW-07 (The generated model routes the deadline through an exclusive gateway, 'Forward case needed', which has no counterpart in the reference. It also omits the timed 'Reminder is due' catch event between the event-based gateway and the follow-up task, so the deadline is not a wait on the event-based gateway. The description states that the deadline is a time that must be waited for before the follow-up )

same as LRN-022 (Reference task "make booking" has no counterpart. The generator instead produced "Book payment" (X4), which paraphrases the action and takes its object from the received money. The description's own verb and object should have been kept. The learned guideline LRN-022 already covers this, so the new guideline only restates it for the case where a preceding receipt event tempts a different noun.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description ends a choice with alternative outcomes, where each outcome is a named action performed on the item (for example approving it or discarding it), and the generated model connects that outcome branch directly to an end event: Model each named outcome action as its own task on its branch, placed after the choice gateway and before the end event that closes the process. The end event follows the task and does not replace it. Do not use the end event label to carry the action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a named action on the item (such as closing it, booking a payment for it, or forwarding it to another party) as the last step of a branch, and the branch then ends the process or the case

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant carries out a named closing action as the last step before the process ends (for example closing or concluding the whole process after the final outcome), and this action is not a gateway condition or a flow label: Model that closing action as its own task on the sequence flow immediately before the end event, so the task performs the work and the end event only marks termination. Do not replace the stated action with an end event alone, and do not leave it out.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that after a awaited occurrence is received (such as a payment), the participant performs a named action of its own (such as making a booking) and then closes the case, so the outcome is a closing action followed by the end of the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description mentions an outside party only as the recipient of a request the company sends, or as the target of a case the company hands over, and never describes that party's own actions as a process participant: Do not create a pool for that outside party and do not draw message flows to or from it. Model the sending of the request or the handover as a task in the company's own process, and model any awaited reply as an intermediate catch event or event-based gateway in that same process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description mentions an outside party only as the recipient of a request the company sends, or as the target of a case the company hands over, and never describes that party's own actions as a process participant

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that after a request is sent, the process waits for one of several occurrences, and that if a stated deadline passes without one of them, a follow-up action is taken: Model the wait as an event-based gateway with one outgoing branch per occurrence the process can receive. Model the deadline as its own branch that starts with a timer intermediate catch event, placed directly after the event-based gateway, and that leads to the follow-up action. Do not replace the deadline branch with an exclusive gateway that tests whether the deadline has passed, and do not connect the gateway directly to the follow-up action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that after a request is sent, the process waits for one of several occurrences, and that if a stated deadline passes without one of them, a follow-up action is taken

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a participant's action on an object and follows it with a prepositional complement or qualifier that names the recipient, purpose or scope of the action (for example 'to ...' or 'for ...'), or with a determiner or modifier that is part of the stated action: Label the task with the verb-object phrase as the description words it, keeping the prepositional complement, qualifier and determiner or modifier that belong to the stated action. Do not shorten the label to the bare verb and object, and do not drop the complement that says to whom, for what or in which scope the action is performed.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant performs a further action after a received amount, naming it with its own verb and object (for example, making a booking), and the generated model would otherwise label the task with a different noun or verb taken from the preceding receipt or from a paraphrase

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description is written in the first person as the account of one performing role that carries out the process's own steps, and the other parties it mentions (such as the party it sends requests to or receives replies from) are never described as having modeled steps of their own: Model the performing role as its own bpmn:participant pool inside a bpmn:collaboration, and place all of the process's start and end events, tasks, gateways and intermediate events in that pool. Do not create a pool for the other parties mentioned, and do not draw message flows to or from them unless the description states a message exchange. Model any reply the process must wait for as an intermediate catch event or event-based gateway inside the performer's pool.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description is written in the first person as the account of one performing role that carries out the process's own steps, and the other parties it mentions (such as the party it sends requests to or receives replies from) are never described as having modeled steps of their own
